definition.def: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.
examples: The striker attributes the team's success to a positive ethos at the club. [VERB noun + to]

definition.def: If you attribute a particular quality or feature to someone or something, you think that they have got it.
examples: People were beginning to attribute superhuman qualities to him. [VERB noun + to]

definition.def: If a piece of writing, a work of art, or a remark is attributed to someone, people say that they wrote it, created it, or said it.
examples: This, and the remaining frescoes, are not attributed to Giotto. [be VERB-ed + to]
...a Madonna and Child attributed to Pietro Lorenzetti. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: An attribute is a quality or feature that someone or something has.
examples: Cruelty is a normal attribute of human behaviour.
He has every attribute you could want and could play for any team.

examples.sentence: I attribute much of my success there to having learned, through the study of mathematics, and, in particular, theorems, how to analyze complicated principles.
Djoser is thought to have reigned for 19 years, but some historians and scholars attribute a much longer time for his rule, owing to the number and size of the monuments he built.
It is hard to dispute that having faith in the capacity to change is a good attribute for students.
We can, perhaps, attribute mediocre results to an inadequate placebo effect.
Now, of course, all essays are based on research done by other people, but you must remember to attribute the work to the original writer.
